content:
jordan: Hey folks — just got an escalated ticket. Customer says when they bundle our TS SDK into their Next.js SSR build they intermittently hit 401s and a flood of retries. They traced it to the client being undefined in prod bundle sometimes. Repro steps below.

sara: Ugh. Do we have their repo/stack? Next version?

jordan: Next 13.4, esbuild via Turbopack. Repro: 1) install @redwood/inference@0.14.2 2) import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference' in api route 3) build and run in prod mode 4) request -> sometimes throws `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a constructor` then SDK retries auth -> 401 -> client spams retry loop.

kai: Could be conditional exports/dual entrypoint mismatch (CJS vs ESM) + tree-shaking in prod bundler. If the import ends up resolving to an empty module that explains runtime undefined.

sara: Can you paste their package.json exports field?

jordan: They shared this snippet: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

jordan: Also tsconfig "module": "ESNext" and they use `type": "module"` at top-level.

support-ops: Noted. Customer says local dev (next dev) is fine, only prod build. That points at bundler optimization.

kai: Another pattern: when bundlers perform namespace hoisting, default vs named import differences can surface. If our package exports a CommonJS module but they `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` it might end up as undefined. Our docs recommend `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` for CJS default interop but that's not ideal.

sara: Is this a packaging regression? Any recent change to exports map or types field?

jordan: We shipped a change last week to add an `exports."./runtime"` entry and adjusted build pipeline to emit `index.mjs` and `index.cjs`. Maybe the exports map resolution edge case wasn't fully covered.

kai: Quick repro I ran: bundling a tiny Next SSR route with esbuild and our package sometimes rewrites the import to `./dist/esm/index.js` but tree-shakes the class constructor into `exports.RedwoodClient = undefined` because of circular re-export ordering between index and runtime. That happens only under production minify.

sara: Potential fixes: 1) ensure stable named exports (avoid live circular re-exports), 2) provide a single interoperable entrypoint (umd or an ESM with named exports guarantee), 3) add a compatibility README block showing correct import patterns for common bundlers.

jordan: Customer wants a short workaround they can patch now.

kai: Workaround options: - Force CJS resolution by pinning `@redwood/inference` to require-style: `const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference/dist/cjs')` or set Next config to transpile to commonjs for our package. - Or change their import to `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.js'` and use Redwood.RedwoodClient. Ugly but quick.

sara: Can we also mitigate the retry storm server-side? If client missing constructor triggers immediate failures we should make server treat auth 401s from malformed clients as non-retryable for a short window to avoid billing/alert storms.

devex-bot: automated-scan: flagged package export surface change in v0.14.2 vs v0.14.1 — added "./runtime" and restructured dist layout.

jordan: I ran a small patch locally: re-export everything from a single file with explicit named exports (no re-export from runtime) -> rebuild -> Next prod build stable. So likely circular re-export ordering.

kai: Action items: 1) rollback or hotfix packaging to guarantee stable named exports in next patch; 2) publish compatibility note for bundlers (esbuild/Turbopack/webpack/rollup) with examples; 3) support ops to apply temporary server-side non-retry tag for effected customer while we patch.

sara: I'll own the patch. jordan can you open a minimal repro repo we can run in CI? Keep it tiny: Next + our SDK + simple SSR route. Put it in mono/repros/so-and-so and link.

jordan: On it. I'll create repro and post link shortly. Also adding a PR with packaging test to our release pipeline to catch this pattern (minified prod bundle of Next + package check).

support-ops: Customer updated: they applied the `require('@redwood/inference/dist/cjs')` workaround and errors dropped. They're waiting on a proper patch.

kai: Nice. For the server side, I've added a temporary rate limit on repeated 401s per origin for 10m and flagged billing team so they can exclude the spike from invoices if needed.

jordan: Thanks team. I'll post the repro link and PR once ready. Closing here when patch published. :thumbsup:
